text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- German goverment spokesman calls decision by Russian President Boris Yeltsin to veto draft law claiming ownership of art booty seized from Nazi Germany during World War Two "an internal Russian affair", but says still working on a compromise that will suit both sides.
- Politicians criticise hostile take over plans of Thyssen by Krupp as thousands of steel workers protest against the move.
- Bavarian Interior Minister Guenter Beckstein accuses the U.S.-based Church of Scientology of trying to infiltrate the Albanian government in 1989 and 1990.
- Opposition Social Democrat (SPD) leader Oskar Lafontaine wants to write to Chancellor Helmut Kohl to detail conditions for return to talks on planned tax reforms.
- Bonn reacts with outrage at attack on two Turks and an Italian by nine German soldiers.
- Juergen Klinsmann says he is set to leave Bayern Munich at the end of the season.
- Cabinet agrees on 25 billion mark investment programme launched by Chancellor Kohl last week.
HANDELSBLATT
- Krupp head Gerhard Cromme wants to take over Thyssen for more than 13 billion marks and offer 435 marks for each Thyssen share.
- Steel workers lay down tools at Thyssen in protest at threat of Krupp takeover which they fear will lead to thousands of job losses.
- Car maker Audi AG reports the highest sales and pre-tax profit in the company's history, posting 1996 pre-tax profit of 862 million marks and sales of 18.8 billion marks.
- Bundesbank reports record investment deficit in 1996 of almost 47 billion marks with foreign investors staying away from Germany.
- Chemicals giant Bayer AG announces 1996 dividend of 1.70 marks, up from 1.40 marks in 1995.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Merger of steel companies sparks fear of mass layoffs. Thyssen accuses predator Krupp of "wild west tactics".
- Defence minister Volker Ruehe defends German army from accusations of right-wing extremism.
- Economics Minster Guenter Rexrodt says planned credit programme of 25 billion marks should create jobs.
- Bavaria's Beckstein calls on the government and states to systematically observe the Church of Scientology.
- Klinsmann set to leave Bayern Munich at end of season.
DIE WELT
- Thyssen fights hostile take over plans by Krupp.
- Chancellor Kohl plans cabinet reshuffle which could mean Economics Minister Rexrodt is replaced by junior coalition partner Free Democrat (FDP) leader Wolfgang Gerhardt.
- Defence Minister Ruehe apologises to victims of racist attack by German soldiers.
